title: Bernini
objective: After this level you can describe Bernini's sculpture and his square at St. Peter's.
summary: Bernini froze marble mid-action: David about to throw, with you in Goliath's place, and Daphne turning into a tree. His colonnades at St. Peter's wrap the square like arms.

cards.headline: Stand in front of Bernini's David, and you're Goliath.
cards.body: Bernini carved David in the instant before he hurls the stone, and he meant the viewer to stand where the giant would be. The sculpture isn't just in the room with you. It's aiming at you.

cards.headline: A hero caught mid-throw
cards.body: Bernini's marble David (1623 to 1624) twists like a coiled spring, arms tense on the sling, the stone about to fly. You get the split second before the action, not a pose after it. There's a personal touch too: according to early sources, David's face is Bernini's own. Standing in Goliath's spot, you're looking at the sculptor's determination.

cards.fact: Bernini made marble turn into a tree.
cards.context: In Apollo and Daphne (1622 to 1625), the god Apollo finally reaches the nymph he's chasing, and she's already changing into a laurel tree. Roots grow from her feet. Leaves sprout from her fingers. Where Apollo's hand lands, there's bark. It's one block of stone, caught in the middle of becoming something else.

mascot.line: Look at her fingertips: stone pretending to be skin, pretending to be leaves.

cards.headline: A square that hugs you
cards.body: Bernini also designed the colonnades of St. Peter's Square in Rome (1656 to 1667): 284 columns in four rows, curving around the square. They symbolize the Church's arms embracing the faithful. And there's a trick. From either of two marble discs in the pavement, the four rows line up and look like one. Remember Pozzo's disc in Level 41? Baroque Rome loved a sweet spot.

questions.prompt: Where did Bernini mean the viewer of his David to stand?

options.label: Behind David, watching over his shoulder
options.rationale: You face him, as his target.

options.label: Far above, looking down from a balcony
options.rationale: You're at ground level, in the fight.

options.label: Beside David, as a fellow soldier
options.rationale: He's aiming at you, not with you.

questions.explanation: The viewer takes Goliath's place, so the throw is aimed right at you.

questions.prompt: What do Bernini's David and his Apollo and Daphne have in common?

options.label: Both show a calm figure at rest
Both freeze a split second in the middle of the action
Both show a story after it has ended
options.rationale: He picks the instant during, not after.

questions.explanation: David is about to throw; Daphne is halfway into a tree. Bernini catches the story while it's happening.

questions.prompt: Pozzo's church (Level 41) and St. Peter's Square both have a special spot in the floor. What happens on the square's disc?

options.label: The four rows of columns line up and look like one
The square's fountain goes silent

questions.explanation: From either marble disc, Bernini's four rows of columns line up into what looks like a single row.
